reason: The scoped tool registry, restrictions, step-time activation and the guarded invocation pipeline are kept as the Go tools component; the in-house schema language is replaced by one Go declaration per tool whose types yield the schema, the validator and the catalogue.

The registry of prompt sections, variables, runtime contexts and the per-step assembly is kept as the prompt component; the whole-assembly waterfall and the change event are replaced by three closed operations.
The native executor is 35 lines that select the shared batch scheduler for a scope; in Go the scheduler is a fixed part of the tools component because the replaceable executor seam is dropped.

Running model-written TypeScript programs is not built (owner decision DH-ADR-8); its purpose, many tool calls in one model step with every call checked and logged, is served by the tool endpoint that scripts reach through the dsh tool command line.

The advisory repeat-call reminder is kept with the same thresholds and texts; its chain becomes a session projection folded from the log instead of an in-memory map, and an optional deny guard is added.
The optional deadline wrapper becomes part of the execute stage of the pipeline, which gives every call a budget and enforces it without a separate component.
The todo_write tool, the todo/write whole-list event and the todos projection are kept with the same contract as a Go component.

Persona prefix and suffix are live fields of the prompt component's config struct, so the generic settings form and the one writable config layer edit prompt text at run time and the next step uses it; no separate prompt-editing API is needed.
The Go interpolation syntax has an inline escape: four opening braces render two literal braces, and a section can still be marked literal as a whole.

Every compiled-in tool name is known to the binary, so config load rejects a toolOrder name that is neither compiled in nor under a declared dynamic prefix, with file and line; a known but hidden name is skipped at assembly instead of failing every turn.

An in-process tool body must still observe cancellation: Go cannot stop a goroutine. The harm is bounded: third-party tool code no longer runs in the host, every first-party body must pass a cancellation conformance test, and after a grace period the call settles as outcome unknown with the body tracked as detached.
justification: No Go mechanism kills a goroutine, so the limit cannot be removed for in-process bodies. Decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-5 bounds its effect to one call and reports it; DH-D-TOOLS-3 builds the bounded wait, the detached list and the conformance helper.

reason: A script selects images with the attach flag on a nested call; the host appends that result's image blocks to the outer result by attachment reference, which works for any image-producing tool and needs no special Image value.
The script never reads the image file: the host attaches the stored image itself, so no mapping from host attachments to program-readable paths exists and the SSH filesystem case cannot arise.
A reset control is needed only because a retained JavaScript (Node) process keeps variables between programs; the Go design has no interpreter and keeps no program state between scripts.
The harness imposes no script language, and reach (direct, script or both) is declared per tool, so one agent can have tools that are callable only directly and tools callable only from scripts.

Each nested result is bounded by maxNestedValueBytes before it is returned to the script and its shaped content is logged as a tool/subresult event, so intermediate results are both bounded and present in the session log.
The limit describes the evaluation modes of the Node vm guest runtime (fresh, persistent in memory, script persistence); with no JavaScript runtime a script keeps state only in files it writes.

The parallel classifier stays on the declaration and operator config can force named tools exclusive; nothing can force a tool parallel, the same one-way rule as guards, so policy outside the tool's owner can tighten scheduling.
A policy listener still cannot rewrite a call's arguments: the Go Call type exposes them read-only and no decision type carries replacement arguments.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-3: outcome DH-O-6 requires logged arguments to stay as written so that history, audit, UI and execution agree. A rewrite would have to happen before the assistant message is committed, which is a driver feature and not a pipeline stage.

reason: In the tools contract a declaration's output type may be any JSON root and the shared schema package has no root restriction; whether subagent and workflow consumers keep an object-root guard is an open question for areas A11 and A12.
The declared timeout is enforced by the execute stage of the pipeline itself; no separate wrapper has to be mounted for a deadline to apply.
A declaration may supply RepeatKey(args), so the tool that knows what counts as the same call defines the identity; the default stays exact canonical JSON.
The chain is a projection folded from the session log and resets on the compaction event, because after compaction the model no longer sees the earlier identical calls.
An optional blockAt count registers a deny-only guard that refuses the call at that run length; it is off by default so the reminder stays advisory unless the operator asks otherwise.
Repeat chains stay per session: a parent and its subagent repeating the same call are still counted separately.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-9: a chain describes one model's own context, and a subagent has a different context, so their calls are not one loop. DH-D-TOOLS-7 builds the per-session projection.

reason: A polling tool declares itself RepeatExempt, so the exemption ships with the tool instead of depending on each deployment's exclude list.
The repeatEvery setting reminds again every N identical calls after the highest threshold, so a long chain no longer goes silent.

The timeout result reaches the model after a bounded grace period whether or not the body returned, and a body that owns a process is stopped by the process stop sequence; a body that still ignores cancellation is detached and reported as outcome unknown.
Every call has a budget: the tool's own, an operator override or the configured default; opting out needs an explicit NoDeadline declaration that a golden test lists.

The todo list still belongs to one agent session; there is no subagent, shared or team list, and a call with no attributed agent fails. A nested call from a script is attributed to its agent and writes that agent's list.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: one owner per list keeps the event a plain last-write-wins snapshot; other sessions' lists are read through their own projections. DH-D-TOOLS-8 builds it.

reason: A todo item is still only content plus a three-state status, with no id, priority or active-form field.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: whole-list replacement needs no item identity, and a smaller shape costs fewer tokens on every write. DH-D-TOOLS-8 builds it.

reason: Whole-list replacement is still the only todo operation: no partial update, per-item edit or read-back tool.
justification: Kept on purpose by decision DH-ADR-TOOLS-10: a whole-list event needs no merge and replays as last write wins, which is the design rule for state-carrying session events, and the model already holds the list in its context. DH-D-TOOLS-8 builds it.

reason: The marker asks for image tools to declare how their result is adapted for a JavaScript program; no program result adaptation exists without the JavaScript guest runtime.
The marker concerns return types in the generated TypeScript SDK for programs; the Go design generates no TypeScript declarations.
The marker is about renaming an npm package before a tagged release; in Go the deadline is a stage of the pipeline and has no package of its own to name.
The Go harness exposes no run_code tool because it has no embedded interpreter; the model runs an ordinary script with the shell tool and the script calls tools through the tool endpoint.
The Go harness exposes todo_write with the same name, arguments and result text.

No around event runs over the assembly; a component changes the prompt by a scoped shadow of a section or variable, by Suppress, or by one Complete section, so the owner of every piece of text stays known.
The prompt is rebuilt for every step and upstream has no shipped listener for this event; the Go prompt component publishes no change event until a consumer needs one.
Replaced by the typed notify key tools.Changed, sent after a registration or restriction change commits.
Replaced by the typed around key tools.Execute; a wrapper may only pass on a context derived from the one it received and cannot change the call.
Replaced by the typed around key tools.Shape, which returns a closed PostDecision (Accept, ReplaceContent, ReplaceValue, Block) and runs for nested calls as well.
Replaced by the typed around key tools.Decide, which returns a closed PreDecision (Allow, Deny, Ask, Cancel) over a read-only call.

A nested call passes the same shape stage as any call, so the listeners that shape a result (such as the spill policy) already shape the logged copy of a nested result and no separate log-copy event is needed.
Replaced by the typed notify key tools.Settled with immutable payloads; observer failures are contained.
Replaced by the config struct of the guard.repeat component: thresholds, include, exclude and argumentsPreviewChars as upstream, plus repeatEvery and blockAt.
Replaced by the config struct of the prompt component with the same five fields; toolOrder names are now checked at config load.
The executor's two limits (sub-calls per minute, parallel sub-calls) become fields of the tools.endpoint component's config struct, with further bounds on pending calls, value size and connections.
Replaced by the config struct of the tool.todo component with the one required field allowParallelInProgress.
Replaced by the Go interface prompt.Service under the service key prompt.Key: Section, Variable, Context, Suppress, Assemble and Render.
Replaced by the Go interface tools.Service under the service key tools.Key: registration, step view, the three entries into the pipeline and the catalogue.
Kept: a tool describes its call and result card through a closed View interface on its declaration, which gives the server-side HTML templates one switch over a closed set.
Kept: every prompt fact has one owner, interpolation is strict, the persona is an ordinary section and assembly takes a per-agent input.

Changed: the around-dispatch hook is kept, but the deadline is no longer an optional plugin for tools that ask; the pipeline gives every call a budget and enforces it, because an optional safety check is a composition mistake away from being absent.

Kept: every call carries the caller's cancellation as a context and the result codes record whether the body started. Changed: a started body is awaited for a bounded grace period and then detached, instead of without bound.

There is no retained program process to clean up; each nested call resolves policy for its agent when it arrives, so it never runs under stale authority. Whether a running sandboxed command is stopped on a mode change belongs to area A09.
The inspect function belongs to the JavaScript guest; in Go the script's standard output is the selection of what the model sees, and the attach flag selects images from a nested result.
The rule is kept: a size or count bound shortens one result or refuses one nested call and never cancels work that has started, because cancelling hides which actions ran.

The presentation mode with a guest runtime is overruled by DH-ADR-8; what survives is that nested calls pass the full pipeline, are scheduled under the same parallel and exclusive rule and are logged before the outer result.

Kept: a Go tool returns one typed canonical value; the tool endpoint returns it to a script as JSON and reports a failed tool as a distinct outcome that names the tool. The generated TypeScript declaration is not built.

Adopted from the start: every declaration states reach (direct, script, both) and disclosure (full, summary, name, none), the step view resolves both once per step, and a search tool discloses deferred tools through a logged event.

The rewrite feature is not built: the note's own open question (whether a provider accepts a rewritten assistant message on replay) is unanswered and outcome DH-O-6 requires logged arguments to stay as written. The note's constraint, no mutation of the execution's arguments, is kept by the Go types.
The harness runs no program language at all, so there is no supported-language choice to make; a script is written in whatever language the machine has.
Adopted: the Go prompt registry emits no change event, because the prompt is rebuilt each step and an advertised event is a promise with ordering rules and tests to maintain.

title: One declaration per tool, with reach and disclosure as per-tool facts
One pipeline and one scheduler; the replaceable executor is dropped
Fixed stage order; validation first, guards before approval; logged arguments are never rewritten
Every call ends in exactly one bounded result
The pipeline enforces a deadline on every call, waits a bounded time, then detaches
The tool endpoint is a new entry, not a new authority
Nested calls: scheduled under their outer call, bounded per call, visible only through the script's output
Prompt assembly is a pure function with closed ways to change it
The repeat reminder is derived from the log
todo_write stays a whole-list tool owned by one session
A tool is declared once and registered in a scope
Every tool call passes one guarded pipeline
Tool calls have enforced deadlines and never hold a turn
A script calls tools through the tool endpoint, checked and logged like any call
The system prompt and tool list for each step are assembled deterministically
Tools can be disclosed on demand
A repeating agent is reminded, and can be stopped
The model keeps a visible task list
Derived schemas are byte-stable, an out-of-subset schema or duplicate name fails registration, and the catalogue lists each tool once
Scoped shadowing, intersecting restrictions, per-agent visibility and removal on disposal; a failing When publishes no partial step view
All three origins pass the eight stages in the fixed order and no input field skips a stage
Invalid arguments never reach policy, an answerer or the body, every violation is reported, and logged argument bytes equal the bytes received
A guard denial holds under any listener order and precedes approval; Ask without an answerer is denied; a panicking check yields a failure result
Calls overlap up to the one cap, a resource-key conflict is a barrier, exclusive calls run alone, results commit in model order, and cancellation leaves one result per call
Output validation, the closed shaping decisions, the result size ceiling and contained settle observers
Deadline budget precedence, timeout within grace, a budget that pauses outside execution and during nested approval, and the golden NoDeadline list
A body that ignores cancellation is detached after grace, reported as outcome unknown, refused as busy and logged when it returns

A call token is minted only where allowed, attributes without authorising, outlives its call only when the workflow tool hands it to a registered job, is refused when missing, forged or deleted, and never appears in a log
A nested call passes every stage, is not covered by the outer approval, and is logged as a subcall and subresult pair before the outer result
Each nested bound refuses one call and names the bound; nested scheduling follows the parallel and exclusive rule; the token is revoked before the outer result
Hostile traffic on the tool endpoint fails one connection only, the request decoder survives fuzzing, and the socket directory is cleaned up
Golden prompt assembly: fixed inputs give fixed bytes and order; shadow, Suppress and Complete each change only their part; the manifest names each owner
Strict interpolation with an inline escape, toolOrder checked at config load, and a persona edit through the config layer changes the next assembly
Repeat reminders at each threshold and after, reset by user message and compaction, identical on replay of the log, with an optional blocking guard
todo_write validates and appends one whole-list event, the projection follows and clears at turn start, and a call with no agent fails
Import direction: only the tools contract package is imported from outside, and it imports no provider
A deferred tool is found by search, becomes fully disclosed in the next step and after replay, and reach alone decides whether a call is accepted
A real model's tool calls pass the pipeline and the request can be rebuilt from the log
A sandboxed script calls a tool that needs approval, and cannot skip it
A command that ignores termination is stopped at its deadline and leaves no process
A looping script is bounded and the host stays responsive
